description_full: Dutch Bros Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates and franchises drive-thru shops in the United States. The company sells and distributes coffee, coffee-related products, and accessories. It operates through Company-Operated Shops and Franchising and Other segments. The company sells its products under various brands such as Dutch Bros, Dutch Bros Coffee, Dutch Bros Rebel, Dutch Bros, and Blue Rebel. Dutch Bros Inc. was founded in 1992 and is based in Tempe, Arizona.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 28K people. Revenue per employee of $59K ranks in the bottom quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers, with revenue growing 35%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $2K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $644 per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 47× revenue per employee (elevated relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (5/10).
financial_summary: Dutch Bros Inc. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $4.5B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +30% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +8.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 12% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $54M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.70× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 4.1×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 3.0% of the shares.
